title: When the Crown Sings
premise: Dominic Vane, last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that records and trades in impossible things—discovers that the border wards fell because someone sold the country's true name, and the sale is written in her own guild's ledgers. As the stars go out and the kingdom unravels from its edges inward, she must trace the transaction through memory itself, aided by a disgraced royal cartographer who once loved her and may have brokered the deal. To find the door out of a country that no longer exists, Dominic must choose between restoring the name (and erasing everyone who remembers the old world) or letting it die while carrying its memory into whatever comes next. She chooses a third path: singing the crown's forgotten song to make the country exist only as long as someone remembers it—and she becomes the one who remembers.
about_author: Ulyana Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents for institutions that no longer exist. She writes fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet heroism of people who keep records.

chapters.title: The Weight of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the crumbling Ledgerhouse, Dominic catalogs impossible items—a bottled echo, a key to nowhere—while her dying master warns her never to read the sealed final ledger. The stars flicker out at midnight, and every ward-stone in the city goes dark. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in routine; the comfort of order breaking apart.

chapters.title: A Country With No Edges
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The borders are simply gone—roads end in fog where neighboring kingdoms used to be. Refugees arrive claiming their home villages no longer remember them. Dominic opens the sealed ledger and finds an entry dated tomorrow: 'Sale of Name: buyer unknown, broker: R. Calloway.' Emotional beat: vertigo and betrayal; the past is not what she trusted.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Riven Calloway's POV. The disgraced royal cartographer is found half-mad in the map vaults, drawing coastlines that keep unexisting. He recognizes Dominic and confesses he brokered something years ago but cannot remember what—the memory was part of the payment. Emotional beat: guilt without recollection; love complicated by erased sin.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Owe
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following ledger-logic, they learn the country's true name was collateral on a debt the old king incurred, now called due. Every person who forgets becomes a blank-faced 'Unwritten.' Dominic realizes her own childhood memories of her mother are suspiciously perfect—too neat, like entries. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the capital, where the crown still sings faintly each dawn—an automated enchantment holding the last of reality together. The young queen, half-Unwritten herself, rules a court of fading nobles and begs Dominic to fix the ledgers. Emotional beat: duty versus truth; the queen asks to be saved even if saving damns others.

chapters.title: Buyer Unknown
chapters.summary: Riven's POV. Tracking the buyer through trade-routes of memory, they find the purchaser: the neighboring empire didn't buy land—it bought existence, and the brokered debt was Riven's price for saving Dominic's life as a child. His erased memory returns: he chose her over his country. Emotional beat: devastating revelation; loyalty and love revealed as the same wound.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Choir
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Unwritten gather at the border-fog, drawn by the crown's failing song, humming harmonies to names they've lost. Among them, Dominic finds her mother—alive, blank, still humming a lullaby that matches the crown's melody. The song and the lullaby are the same song. Emotional beat: heartbreak transmuted into hope; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dominic confronts the empire's envoy at the fog-line: the contract can be voided if the name is returned willingly or sung by a living voice who holds it whole. But singing it will burn the singer's own memories as fuel. Riven offers himself; Dominic refuses to let him pay alone. Emotional beat: sacrifice negotiated between lovers; duty finally chosen freely.

chapters.title: When the Crown Sings
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At dawn, before the dead court and the Unwritten choir, Dominic sings the country's true name with the crown and her mother's lullaby braided together. Reality knits back—stars, borders, faces—but her memories feed the song, unraveling as she sings. Riven holds her, giving her his memories of them so she doesn't vanish mid-note. Emotional beat: climax; love literally carrying memory across the void.

chapters.title: The One Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue-toned. The country exists again—but fragile, sustained only because Dominic carries its full memory, making her both keeper and keystone. She reopens the Ledgerhouse, takes apprentices, and writes the first honest entry: the whole truth about the sale, including Riven's choice. He stays, learning to love her again alongside new memories. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory as both burden and home.
